claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a continuous dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The initial alloy has less than 5% room-temperature elongation and is prone to catastrophic interfacial cracking.
Severe plastic deformation produces massive dislocation density and fragments the continuous lamellae.
Partial or phase-selective recrystallization after deformation can retain ultrafine deformed regions while producing coarser recrystallized regions.
Annealing at 600-750 °C for 10-30 minutes followed by water quenching will create the proposed heterogeneous structure.
The extreme-pressure deformation variant requires pressure above 1.5 GPa.
The resulting heterogeneous structure will contain ultrafine grains of 0.5-2 μm and coarse grains of 10-30 μm.
The proposed treatment will generate a high density of coherent internal boundaries, including nanotwins or coherent phase interfaces, within lamellar fragments.
Fragmenting the lamellae eliminates long, continuous brittle interfaces that serve as crack-propagation paths.
A heterogeneous grain structure generates back-stress hardening through geometrically necessary dislocations at boundaries.
Back-stress hardening delays necking and promotes uniform plasticity.
Coherent internal boundaries facilitate dislocation dissociation and storage.
Coherent boundaries enhance strain-hardening capacity without sacrificing strength.
The proposed heterogeneous structure will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in AlCoCrFeNi.
The treated AlCoCrFeNi alloy will have uniform elongation greater than 20%.
The treated AlCoCrFeNi alloy will have an ultimate tensile strength greater than 1.5 GPa.
Treatment will reduce microcrack density and change failure from interfacial cleavage to ductile void coalescence.
Annealing below 600 °C will provide insufficient recrystallization, whereas annealing above 750 °C will cause full recrystallization and loss of heterogeneous strengthening.
More than 50% deformation reduction is required to fragment the lamellae.
Conventional HIP at 1000 °C and 100 MPa for two hours promotes full recrystallization and grain growth without severe deformation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis defines the extreme-pressure variant as deformation above 1.5 GPa, but Set A is specified only as cold rolling plus annealing and Set B uses HIP at 0.1 GPa. Thus the proposed comparison does not vary extreme pressure in isolation, despite the falsification rule describing it as a test of whether extreme pressure/deformation is required.
